validity.researcher_notes: Built the case from primary sources, not just the roster's flagged suspicion. Three independent FERC Federal Register notices for Docket No. CP15-504-000 (Dominion Carolina Gas Transmission, LLC's application) all state the SAME project is 'approximately 28-mile[s]' / 'approximately 28 miles of new 8-inch-diameter... pipeline': the Notice of Application (2015-15092, 2015-06-19), the Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review (2015-31720, 2015-12-17), and the EA Notice of Availability (2016-04143, 2016-02-26) -- 28 mi x 1.60934 = 45.06 km, an essentially exact match to P2649's recorded 45.00 km. Meanwhile the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx, 'Historical Projects' tab) carries exactly ONE database record for this same Docket CP15-504 project -- Operator 'Dominion Carolina Gas Transmission', Project Name 'Columbia to Eastover Pipeline', Miles=29, Diameter=8in, Additional Capacity=18 MMcf/d, Cost=$36M, Completed Date 2016-11-01 -- and the Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Planned Projects in the Americas' (Nov. 2016 PDF, entry 'DOMINION CAROLINA -- (7/16) Project: Columbia to Eastover Pipeline') independently repeats the identical 29-mile/South Carolina/2016-completion/18-MMcf/d figures. So there are two internally-consistent clusters of sourcing for what is, per every document, ONE FERC docket and one physical pipeline: a 28-mi/45-km cluster (3 FERC Federal Register notices, matching P2649 as recorded) and a 29-mi cluster (EIA's compiled database + PGJ trade-press digest, matching P4381's recorded roster values almost exactly). The 1-mile gap (28 vs 29 mi, 3.6%) is consistent with a proposed-vs-as-built mileage refinement on the SAME line, not two different pipelines -- no FERC document, EIA record, or trade-press mention anywhere in this pass describes a SECOND Columbia-to-Eastover-area pipeline, a second CP-docket, or a second capacity/purpose distinct from the one 18,000-dekatherm/day (=18 MMcf/d) firm-service delivery to the International Paper plant in Eastover, SC. Every other attribute lines up identically across both rows per the batch roster: same owner (Carolina Gas Transmission / Dominion Carolina Gas Transmission), same capacity (18 MMcf/d), same completion year (2016), same 8-inch diameter, same South Carolina location. This is strong, multi-source, primary-document evidence for a double-counted row, not merely the pre-existing roster suspicion restated.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Sheet's LastUpdated is 2023-08-14. The most recent PROJECT-SPECIFIC dated evidence found is from 2016 (the FERC Sec. 4(d) rate filing putting the Columbia-to-Eastover transportation service into effect 11/1/2016, and EIA's Completed Date of 2016-11-01) -- I found no post-2018 document that names this specific 28/29-mile lateral by name. However: (1) the current owner's corporate site (bhegts.com/our-businesses/CGT, accessed 2026-09-10 -- three years newer than LastUpdated) describes the whole CGT system, of which this lateral is a permanent physical part, in the present tense as an operating ~1,500-mile interstate pipeline with no mention of any lateral being idled, abandoned, or retired; (2) this is a short (28-29 mi), small-diameter (8in) firm-service delivery lateral built specifically to serve one large industrial customer (the International Paper plant in Eastover, SC) under a FERC-approved negotiated-rate transportation contract -- this is exactly the class of asset that, once built and placed in FERC tariff service, has no natural retirement trigger short of the customer closing or relocating, and no news, FERC docket, or SEC filing search this pass turned up any indication of the Eastover IP plant closing or the lateral being abandoned; (3) I could not locate a PHMSA operator-level annual report or a post-2018 FERC docket specific to just this lateral within this pass's search scope. On balance: no evidence of change, circumstantial evidence of continuity (parent system verifiably still operating in 2026, no closure/abandonment signal found for the specific delivery customer), so verdict is 'confirm' -- but flagging tier as medium rather than high because the newest evidence naming THIS specific segment by name is from 2016, not post-LastUpdated.
